title: Power Screw Workbench
summary: Compare the geometry, torque and back-driving behaviour of a power screw using an interactive preliminary model. The workspace ties thread inputs to numerical results, an unwrapped-thread explanation and a 3D view, then keeps named design runs for comparison.
features: Load, major diameter, starts, thread angle, pitch or helix angle, and mean-diameter basis.
Screw/nut material, manufacturing process, lubrication and supplier/measured friction override.
Optional collar friction and mean collar diameter.
Raising torque, back-drive/lowering behaviour, efficiency and disclosed assumptions.
Orbit, zoom, side/end views, rotation and equivalent nut advance; compare thread starts.
Named comparisons and Excel XML, Excel-compatible and JSON exports.
workflows: Give the run a name, then enter axial force in N and dimensions in mm. Do not enter mass where a force is requested.
Select Pitch or Helix angle as the independent input. Check thread starts: lead is starts multiplied by pitch, so one turn can advance more than one pitch.
Use a measured/supplier mean diameter when available instead of silently treating the preliminary estimate as a standard thread specification.
Open Materials and choose the relevant material/process/lubrication conditions. Replace estimated friction with measured or supplier values when available.
Enable Collar only when the intended assembly has that friction contribution and enter its mean diameter and coefficient.
Read the thread-alone and total screw-plus-collar results separately. Expand the equations and sign convention before interpreting a negative lowering torque.
Change one input at a time and save named runs. A back-drivable result depends on the entered assumptions; it is not a brake or safety-system approval.
Orbit the 3D screw or choose Side/End and use rotation to see equivalent nut advance. The shown length/root diameter also affect the illustration.
Expand Compare 2, 3 & 4 starts and the unwrapped-thread diagrams to understand why a geometry change changes lead and torque.
Save run, export JSON for restorable data, and use Excel-compatible outputs for a report. Restore JSON when continuing on another browser.
limits: This is a preliminary geometry/friction model. It does not replace checking buckling, fatigue, thread strength, lubrication variation and the actual assembly. No new engineering validation was performed during documentation work.
